summary: Toronto tenants have the right to a comfortable and healthy home. During last September's heatwave some residents reported temperature readings of over 30 degrees Celsius in their units as a result of their landlords turning on heat and/or not turning on air conditioning. Central air conditioning acts as ventilation in many older 'tower block' apartment buildings. If the air conditioning is turned off, there is effectively no ventilation within apartment units. In response to the suffering of many Torontonians, Council unanimously endorsed a motion to direct the Executive Director, Municipal Licensing and Standards, in consultation with other appropriate divisions, to hold consultations with tenants, landlords and other relevant stakeholders to identify potential solutions to effectively deal with heat in apartment buildings, including maximum heat in apartments and applicable dates in the heating bylaw and property standards bylaw, and to report back to the Tenant Issues Committee in the first quarter of 2018. While there was a presentation on extreme heat in apartment buildings presented to Tenant Issues Committee, no recommendations were provided. The item was then brought to the Executive Committee where a request to report on additional items was made, including the development of a strategy to ensure that landlords do not exacerbate tenant discomfort through not turning…
decided: City Council on April 24, 25, 26 and 27, 2018, adopted the following: 1. City Council direct the Executive Director, Municipal Licensing and Standards, in consultation with the Medical Officer of Health, who has authority to declare appropriate high temperature days on which landlords can be permitted to turn off heat and, if applicable, turn on air conditioning in conjunction with the existing heat alert system. 2. City Council request the Medical Officer of Health to establish the Heat Relief Network to promote locally available air-conditioned public spaces, as described in a presentation from Municipal Licensing and Standards to the February 9, 2018 meeting of the Tenant Issues Committee.
